title: Set each grade's voice on purpose
statement: Set each grade's voice, tone, praise, feedback length and pace on purpose for its learners' age, and never let a missing setting fall back to another grade's default.
example: A Grade 5 lesson almost shipped in grade 4's child voice and storytime pace, which the code's own comment called silent and plausible.
detail: The reading project's audio conventions found no grade 9 entry in its voice table, so new clips would silently fall through to grade 4's child voice and storytime pace, the same mistake that almost shipped for Grade 5 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0194-g3-book-audio-clip-conventions.qmd`). A Grade 5 rebuild passed every content validator and its unit test, yet its live page broke because a helper hard-coded grade 3 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0193-g3-book-grade-agnostic-vs-specific-g9-checklist.qmd`). The same transfer checklist found that the Grade 5 build's register (no "You did it!", no medals or confetti, ≤40-word feedback, hedging allowed) was a content standard that lived in the page files, never in the renderer, and it puts a new grade's own register standard first. Keep each grade's register in a standard of its own, apart from the shared code; a fallback to another grade's default looks plausible and is wrong.

evidence.quote: **No grade-9 entry exists.** Without one, G9 clips would silently fall through to `DEFAULT_VOICES`/`DEFAULT_STYLE` = grade 4's child voice and storytime pace — "silent and plausible," per this same file's own comment about the identical mistake almost shipping for Grade 5 ("a ten-year-old reading about salinity gradients would have been read to as if this were a bedtime story").
a G5 rebuild passed every content validator and its unit test, yet the live page silently broke, because `bookCompoundResume.ts`'s `frameBlankInput()` hard-coded `grade: 3`
